children: North Macedonia’s industrial production increased 1.3% year-on-year in July 2026, slowing sharply from 6.5% in the previous month.

Output growth eased in manufacturing (3.4% vs 7.9% in June), particularly for food products, textiles, wearing apparel, and other transport equipment, while declines deepened in mining and quarrying (-5.9% vs -3.8%) and electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply (-19.5% vs -8.2%).
By industrial grouping, production fell for capital goods (-2.9% vs 8.6%) and durable consumer goods (-9.9% vs 8.6%), while the decline in energy deepened (-22.2% vs -11.1%).
Output of intermediate goods excluding energy also slowed (9.2% vs 11.7%).
In contrast, output of non-durable consumer goods rose faster (3.1% vs 2.0%).
In the January-July period, industrial output increased 0.9% from the corresponding period a year earlier.

title: North Macedonia Industrial Output Growth Eases in July
